key_insight: A proposed dual-species atom-array architecture uses global driving and atom-mediated selectivity to enable universal fault-tolerant quantum computation without locally addressed quantum gates.
engineering_relevance: Replacing local gate addressing could reduce control complexity and associated calibration requirements in large-scale neutral-atom quantum processors.
method: Use interspecies Rydberg interactions to selectively control qubits under global driving.
Construct a universal native instruction set: Global Rydberg Atom Instruction Language (GRAIL).
Compile surface-code error correction and magic state cultivation into GRAIL, parallelizing operations to suppress crosstalk.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports crosstalk suppression to the 10^-4 level and, under a hardware-inferred circuit-level noise model, a 1.43% quantum-memory threshold and cultivated magic-state logical error below 10^-9.
watch_item: The reported fault-tolerance performance is model-based; experimental validation must establish that global control and dual-species interactions sustain the assumed noise levels at scale.
paper_title: A Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Architecture with Globally Driven Atom Arrays
